annotations.title: Check a source is who they say they are

description: Someone says they are a doctor, a lawyer, a broker, a professor, a director of a company. This checks those particular claims against the official lists that would record them. Paste whatever you have — the pitch email, a name, a link — and the claims are read out of it. You get one of four answers: verified, partly verified, could not verify, or contradicted by the record. Under it: each claim that was confirmed, where it was confirmed and a link to the entry; each claim that was not, saying exactly which list was searched and came back empty; and a plain list of what was not checked at all, so a gap looks like a gap instead of a clean bill of health. It will never tell you somebody is fake. There is no such answer, because failing to find someone on a list is not evidence they are lying — plenty of real people are not on the list that would cover them, and "could not verify" means one search, on one day, in one place. What comes back is fixed at the moment it was made and never edited; checking again later produces a new one and leaves the first alone. Use it for "is this person who they say they are", "check this expert before I quote them", "should I trust this pitch", "is this doctor actually registered". Costs 25 credits and takes a few seconds.

employer.description: Optional. The organisation they say they are with, if it is not obvious from the input.

input.description: The pasted pitch, name, email address or link naming the person to check. Paste it whole — the claims are read out of it.

name.description: Optional. The subject's name, if it is not obvious from the input.

title.description: Optional. The role or credential they state, if it is not obvious from the input.

name: source_check

balance_credits_before.description: The credit balance before this check.

checks.description: Each claim checked: what was claimed, where it was looked up, what was found and a link to the entry.

citation.description: A line to cite this check by.

created_at.description: When the check was made (ISO date and time).

credits_charged.description: Credits this call took. 0 when nothing was charged.

credits_returned.description: Credits given back when the check could not finish.

error.description: Present when the call could not do the work; says why and that nothing was charged where that is so.

message.description: A plain note about the answer, for example why candidates were returned instead of a result.

not_checked.description: Claims that were not checked at all, so a gap reads as a gap.

ok.description: True when the check ran and was saved.

pricing_note.description: What this call cost and what a repeat costs.

report_id.description: Id of the saved check. A check is never edited; checking again makes a new one.

report_ref.description: Short reference to quote for this check.

subject.description: Who the check is about, as read from the input.

tag.description: A short code for why a check was refused, when it was.

verdict.description: One of: verified, partly verified, could not verify, contradicted by the record.

verdict_sentence.description: The verdict in one plain sentence.

title: Check a source is who they say they are
